theory.intro: The index laws work in exactly the same way when one or more of the indices is negative: you still add indices when multiplying, subtract when dividing, and multiply when raising a power to a power. The only extra work comes at the end, where a negative index is rewritten as a reciprocal so the answer is left with positive indices.
facts: $a^{m}\times a^{n}=a^{m+n}$, $a^{m}\div a^{n}=a^{m-n}$ and $\left(a^{m}\right)^{n}=a^{mn}$ all hold when $m$ or $n$ is negative.
$a^{-n}=\frac{1}{a^{n}}$, so a result such as $x^{-4}$ is written $\frac{1}{x^{4}}$.
Coefficients are handled separately from the indices — multiply or divide them as ordinary numbers.
A coefficient only takes the index if it is **inside the brackets**: in $3a^{-5}=\frac{3}{a^{5}}$ the $3$ stays put, but in $\left(4w^{-3}\right)^{2}=\frac{16}{w^{6}}$ the $4$ is squared.
steps: Apply the index law to each base, keeping the negative signs.
Rewrite any negative index as a reciprocal so the answer has positive indices.
